final_answer:
Let
\[
A_n=\int_{[0,1]^4}e^{-nT^2}\,d\mathbf x,\qquad B_n=I_n(0).
\]
Then
\[
I_n(\lambda)=A_n\sinh\lambda+B_n,
\]
and since \(A_n>0\), the unique solution satisfies
\[
\sinh\lambda_n=-\frac{B_n}{A_n}.
\]

For any integrable \(f\) depending only on \(T=x_1x_2x_3x_4\),
\[
\int_{[0,1]^4} f(T)\,d\mathbf x
=\frac16\int_0^1 f(t)(-\log t)^3\,dt.
\]
Thus, with \(m=n^{1/3}\),
\[
A_n=\frac16\int_0^1 e^{-nt^2}(-\log t)^3\,dt.
\]
Using \(t=u/\sqrt n\),
\[
A_n\sim \frac16 n^{-1/2}\left(\frac12\log n\right)^3\int_0^\infty e^{-u^2}\,du
=\frac{\sqrt\pi}{96}n^{-1/2}(\log n)^3.
\]

Now write the non-\(\lambda\) part as \(B_n\). Put
\[
h_m(y)=e^{-m[3+(y-1)^2]}-2y e^{-m[3+(y^2-4)^2]}
+\frac{3y^2+2}{2}e^{-m[4+W+W^2]},
\]
where \(W=y^3+2y\). Since \(Y_j=(2n)^{1/3}2^jT=2^{1/3}m2^jT\),
\[
B_n=\frac1{6(2n)^{1/3}}\sum_{j=0}^3(-1)^{3-j}\binom3j
\int_0^{(2n)^{1/3}2^j}h_m(y)
\left(\log((2n)^{1/3}2^j)-\log y\right)^3dy.
\]
The upper limits may be replaced by \(\infty\) with exponentially smaller error. Since
\[
\sum_{j=0}^3(-1)^{3-j}\binom3j(u+j\log2)^3=6(\log2)^3,
\]
we get
\[
B_n\sim \frac{(\log2)^3}{(2n)^{1/3}}H_m,
\]
where
\[
H_m=\int_0^\infty h_m(y)\,dy.
\]

Compute \(H_m\) exactly enough. The first two pieces give
\[
e^{-3m}\left(\int_{-1}^\infty e^{-mu^2}\,du-\int_{-4}^\infty e^{-mv^2}\,dv\right)
=-e^{-3m}\int_1^4 e^{-ms^2}\,ds.
\]
For the third piece, using \(w=y^3+2y\), \(dw=(3y^2+2)dy\),
\[
\int_0^\infty \frac{3y^2+2}{2}e^{-m[4+W+W^2]}\,dy
=\frac{e^{-4m}}2\int_0^\infty e^{-m(w+w^2)}\,dw.
\]
Also
\[
\int_1^4 e^{-ms^2}\,ds
=e^{-m}\int_0^{15}e^{-mr}\frac{dr}{2\sqrt{1+r}}.
\]
Hence
\[
H_m=\frac{e^{-4m}}2\left[
\int_0^\infty e^{-m(w+w^2)}\,dw
-\int_0^{15}e^{-mr}(1+r)^{-1/2}\,dr
\right].
\]
By Watson expansion,
\[
\int_0^\infty e^{-m(w+w^2)}dw=\frac1m-\frac2{m^2}+O(m^{-3}),
\]
while
\[
\int_0^{15}e^{-mr}(1+r)^{-1/2}dr=\frac1m-\frac1{2m^2}+O(m^{-3}).
\]
Therefore
\[
H_m\sim -\frac34 e^{-4m}m^{-2}.
\]
Since \((2n)^{1/3}=2^{1/3}m\),
\[
B_n\sim -\frac{3(\log2)^3}{4\cdot 2^{1/3}}e^{-4n^{1/3}}n^{-1}.
\]

Thus
\[
-\frac{B_n}{A_n}
\sim
\frac{3(\log2)^3}{4\cdot 2^{1/3}}
\cdot \frac{96}{\sqrt\pi}
\frac{e^{-4n^{1/3}}n^{-1}}{n^{-1/2}(\log n)^3}
=
\frac{72(\log2)^3}{2^{1/3}\sqrt\pi}
\frac{e^{-4n^{1/3}}}{n^{1/2}(\log n)^3}.
\]
This tends to \(0\), so \(\lambda_n\sim -B_n/A_n\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{\alpha=\frac12,\qquad \beta=3,\qquad c=4,\qquad
L=\frac{72(\log2)^3}{2^{1/3}\sqrt\pi}}.
\]
